intro: Genres, the parts of a story, and the verbs for talking and writing about books.
p.argumento.consejo: It is the plot of a book or film. In a debate, «argumento» is also a reason, never a quarrel.
p.narrador.consejo: It may speak in the first person («yo») or the third («él»). It is not the same as the author.
p.relato.consejo: It is shorter than a novel. «Relato» and «cuento» are used almost the same. It comes from «relatar», to tell.
p.leyenda.consejo: The ll sounds like y: le-YEN-da. It passes by word of mouth and nobody knows how much is true.
p.ensayo.consejo: Careful: «ensayo» is also the rehearsal of an orchestra or a play. Check the context.
p.capítulo.consejo: It has an accent on the i: ca-PÍ-tu-lo. A book has chapters and so does a television series.
p.desenlace.consejo: It comes from «desenlazar», to untie a knot: the knot of the story comes undone at the end.
p.editorial.consejo: The company is «la editorial». A newspaper's opinion article is «el editorial».
p.agotarse.glosa: to sell out, to run out
p.agotarse.consejo: It takes «se»: «se agotó la edición». It also means running out of strength: «me agoto».
p.tirada.consejo: It comes from «tirar», which also means to print. It is the number of copies of an edition.
p.verso.consejo: It is written with v but sounds like b: BER-so. Several lines in a row make a stanza.
p.rimar.consejo: The ending sounds rhyme: «luna» and «cuna». The initial r is strong: rri-MAR.
p.tratar de.consejo: «El libro trata de un viaje» is the classic way to summarise. «Tratar de» + infinitive means to try.
p.ambientado en.consejo: You say «un relato ambientado en Sevilla». It agrees with the noun: «una novela ambientada en…».
b1.texto:
**Genres.** **Prosa** is running text; **verso** is each line of a poem. In prose there are novels, **relatos** (or cuentos), **leyendas** and **ensayos**. Novels can be historical, adventure, romance (rosa) or crime (negra).

**Inside a story.** The **argumento** is what happens. The **narrador** tells it, in the first or the third person. It can be **ambientado en** a place and a time. Each part is a **capítulo** and the end is the **desenlace**.

**Summarising.** Use the present: «La novela **trata de** un hombre que…», «Es un relato **ambientado en** el Madrid de los años cuarenta».

**The book trade.** The **editorial** publishes or edits the book. The **tirada** is the number of copies; if it sells well, the edition **se agota** (sells out).

**Poetry.** **Versos** rhyme and are recited.

**Careful.** A **librería** sells books; a **biblioteca** lends them.
b2.f0.texto: What is that book you are carrying about?
b2.f1.texto: It is a long tale set in a village in the north.
b2.f2.texto: Who tells the story in the first chapter?
b2.f3.texto: A small boy narrates the events in the first person.
b2.f4.texto: Will you tell me the ending?
b2.f5.texto: I would rather not tell you, because the ending is a surprise.
b2.f6.texto: Has a big publishing house published it?
b2.f7.texto: The first print run has already sold out.
b4.texto:
To summarise a book or a film use the **present**, even if the story is set in the past:

- **La novela trata de** un viaje. (**tratar de** + topic)
- **El relato está ambientado en** una ciudad. (**ambientado en** + place or period)
- **El protagonista es** un joven **que** busca a su hermano. (**que** introduces the character)
- **Cuenta la historia de** una familia. (**contar la historia de**)

With **tratar de**, the topic takes **de**: «trata de amor». With **contar** or **narrar**, it does not: «cuenta un viaje».
b4.e0.texto: The novel is about a journey through the desert.
b4.e1.texto: The tale is set in the Spain of the twenties.
b4.e2.texto: The main character is a young man who is looking for his brother.
b5.f0.texto: In the attic, a yellow lamp lights a manuscript full of crossings-out.
b5.f1.texto: The author rereads the last chapter with a pencil between her teeth.
b5.f2.texto: Outside, the rain taps the glass with a slow, steady rhythm.
b5.f3.texto: Each sentence sounds in her head like an old song.
b5.f4.texto: At last she writes the final line and rests her forehead on the warm pages.
b5.f5.texto: Months later, the publishing house prints a small run with a green cloth cover.
b5.f6.texto: The books arrive in boxes at a neighbourhood bookshop and smell of fresh ink.
b5.f7.texto: A woman in a grey coat opens the first copy and reads the beginning in a low voice.
b5.f8.texto: A customer comes closer slowly and asks about the plot of the book.
b5.f9.texto: A week later, the whole print run has sold out.
b6.o0.refuerzo: The editor prepares the book but does not tell the story inside it.
b6.o1.refuerzo: Yes: the narrator is the voice that tells the story.
b6.o2.refuerzo: The reader reads the story; he does not tell it.
b6.pregunta: Who tells the story in a novel?
b7.o0.refuerzo: Yes: «tratar de» + topic is the formula for summarising a book.
b7.o1.refuerzo: «Cuenta» takes no «de» here: you say «cuenta un viaje».
b7.o2.refuerzo: «Narra» does not take «de» before the topic either.
b7.pregunta: Which verb goes with «de» to summarise?
b8.frase: La primera tirada se agotó en una semana
b8.traduccion: The first print run sold out in a week
b9.o0.refuerzo: In a library books are lent, not bought.
b9.o1.refuerzo: The publishing house publishes the books; it is not the shop.
b9.o2.refuerzo: Yes: the «librería» is the shop where books are sold.
b11.frase: Dos versos ____ cuando terminan con el mismo sonido.
b11.o0.refuerzo: Yes: «rimar» is ending two lines with the same sound.
b11.o1.refuerzo: «Recitar» is saying a poem aloud; it says nothing about equal sounds.
b11.o2.refuerzo: «Tratar de» is being about a topic; it does not fit sounds.
b12.o0: que el autor vive en Madrid
b12.o0.refuerzo: That is about the author; «ambientado» is about the story.
b12.o1: que la historia sucede en Madrid
b12.o1.refuerzo: Yes: «ambientado en» a place means the story takes place there.
b12.o2: que el libro se vende en Madrid
b12.o2.refuerzo: That would be about the sale, not the place of the story.
p.narra.consejo: «Narrar» means to tell a story. The rr at the start of a word is strong.
p.hechos.consejo: The h is silent: E-chos. Think of «hecho», done or fact.
p.cuentas.consejo: «Contar» changes o to «ue»: cuento, cuentas, cuenta.
p.contártelo.glosa: to tell you it (infinitive with pronouns)
p.contártelo.consejo: Pronouns go attached at the end of the infinitive: «contar» + «te» + «lo».
p.publicado.consejo: Words ending in -ado are past participles, like «publicado».
p.buhardilla.consejo: The h is silent, and the ll sounds like «y»: bur-DI-ya. Feminine.
p.manuscrito.consejo: Literally «written by hand». Two words, «manu» and «scriptus», in Latin.
p.tachaduras.consejo: From «tachar», to cross out. The ch sounds like «ch» in «chair».
p.autora.consejo: The feminine of «autor»: «la autora». Note the -a ending.
p.imprime.consejo: «Imprimir» is to print. Its family is «impresora» and «impresión».
p.cubierta.consejo: From «cubrir», to cover. The stress is on BYER.
p.ejemplar.consejo: The j sounds like «h»: e-khem-PLAR. Masculine: «el ejemplar».
p.comienzo.consejo: From «comenzar», to begin. Use «el comienzo» with a masculine article.
p.agotó.consejo: «Agotar» means to use up everything. The stress is on TO.
p.versos.consejo: The v sounds like «b»: BER-sos. «El verso» is masculine.
p.terminan.consejo: Plural form of «terminar». The stress is on MI.
p.riman.consejo: In poetry, lines that «riman» end with the same sound.
p.sucede.consejo: The c before e sounds like «th»: su-THE-de. Stress on THE.
